authored_papers.title: Estimating the Net Effect of Rice Cultivation on Soil Organic Carbon Using Planting Trajectories and Causal Forests
keywords: soil organic carbon; rice cultivation; planting trajectory; causal forest; net effect identification
authored_papers.summary: Rice-growing areas often exhibit elevated soil organic carbon (SOC) levels, yet this observational pattern alone cannot determine whether higher SOC reflects the carbon-sequestration effect of rice cultivation itself or the preferential establishment of rice paddies on sites with favourable water availability and soil fertility. Because conventional machine-learning approaches primarily capture associational patterns and do not explicitly address site-selection bias, the true net carbon-sequestration effect of rice cultivation, together with its spatial heterogeneity, remains poorly quantified at large scales. Here we integrated soil observations across China from 2010 to 2024 (2,942 samples) with nearly two decades of crop distribution data. We developed planting-trajectory metrics to represent long-term cropping history, constructed counterfactual matched samples of rice and non-rice fields under comparable environmental conditions, and applied causal forests to estimate both the net effect of rice cultivation on SOC and its spatial heterogeneity. Incorporating planting trajectories into the base learners of the causal forest substantially improved the representation of SOC variability, increasing R² by 30.4% on average and enhancing the mapped SOC pattern across major grain-producing regions. Trajectory-related variables accounted for 15.3% of cumulative relative importance. The proportion of years under rice cultivation exerted a positive and approximately linear influence on SOC, whereas consecutive rice-cultivation years showed a threshold response at approximately four years: the SOC benefit increased up to this point and declined thereafter, while remaining positive overall. Causal estimates indicated a significant positive net effect of rice cultivation on SOC, with an average treatment effect (ATE) of 1.618 g kg⁻¹ (p < 0.001), corresponding to a relative increase of 19.36% compared to the study-wide mean SOC of 8.356 g·kg⁻¹. Conditional average treatment effects (CATE) exhibited pronounced spatial heterogeneity, with stronger SOC gains in the North China Plain, the Huang-Huai-Hai Plain and the Jianghuai region, highlighting these areas as priority regions for paddy-field optimization and cropland carbon management. Rice-induced SOC gains were promoted by warmer and wetter climatic conditions and weaker topographic constraints, and were greatest in neutral to slightly alkaline, fine-textured, and relatively nutrient-limited soils. In contrast, SOC differences between rice and non-rice systems were smaller in nutrient-rich soils. By integrating long-term cropping history with causal inference, this study advances SOC assessment from association-based prediction towards effect-oriented estimation. It provides a useful observational causal-inference framework for estimating the contribution of cropping systems to soil carbon accumulation and offers new insights for spatially targeted cropland carbon management.

keywords: soil organic carbon; arid and semi-arid regions; spatial prediction; time series environmental variables; accumulation and legacy effect.
authored_papers.summary: The Tianshan Mountains in Xinjiang, China, represent a typical ecologically sensitive region in the arid and semi-arid zone of Central Asia. Accurately mapping soil organic carbon (SOC) in this region and revealing its dominant controlling factors are of great significance for regional carbon assessment and ecological security. Conventional digital soil mapping methods mostly rely on environmental variables from a single year, failing to account for the temporal accumulation effects of environmental factors or the legacy impacts of extreme years. To address this issue, this study utilized 463 soil sampling data points and introduced time-series environmental variables over the past decade, including both single-year variables and multi-year mean variables. Multiple machine learning models were employed to predict the spatial distribution of SOC. The results showed that after introducing a set of time-series variables centered on the second year before sampling, the optimal model’s predictive R² increased from 0.682 to 0.751, and the root mean square error decreased by 18.2%. The SOC in the study area exhibited a pattern of higher values in the north and lower values in the south, with high-value areas showing a V-shaped belt distribution. SHAP analysis revealed contrasting dominant controls: elevation and pH governed SOC in the mountain belt, whereas the soil coloration index dominated in the lowlands. Further analysis of time-series variable importance revealed that both accumulation and legacy effects were concentrated in the time-series variables centered on the second year before sampling. This may be attributed to a compound drought-low temperature anomaly that occurred in that year, which had a persistent impact on vegetation growth and subsequent soil carbon inputs. This study confirms the necessity of incorporating temporal accumulation and legacy effects into SOC prediction and offers a methodological reference for digital SOC mapping in arid and semi-arid regions.

evidence_quotes: DEMands of Precision: How DEM Resolution Shapes Various Flood Applications

Digital elevation models (DEM) form the backbone of flood related studies. Proper selection of the DEM product is critical to obtain reliable estimates. Most studies aimed at understanding DEM resolution impacts focus on geometric comparisons. A comprehensive structural and functional assessment framework for DEM comparisons is developed here. The structural differences in DEM are used to understand how DEM products produce differing estimates of flooding susceptibility, rainfall-runoff partitioning, sediment flux estimates and impacts of pluvial flooding. While there is no single DEM resolution that is superior, the results indicate that the ASTER-based 30m DEM is generally the least reliable. The widely available 10m 3DEP DEM is well suited for rainfall-runoff partitioning and flood risk and susceptibility mapping applications. Resampling this DEM to 15m resolution yields similar results and can be used in large domain applications. LiDAR based high-resolution DEMs (1m or less resolution) are best suited for pluvial flood delineations and stormwater management. Even 10m DEM is noted to yield inconsistent results. The 30m ASTER-based DEM yields the most conservative estimate of sediment fluxes due to overprediction of slope and altered watershed shape. The high resolution DEM is therefore recommended for this application as well.

evidence_quotes: Integrating Physical-Based Xinanjiang Model and Deep Learning for Interpretable Streamflow Simulation: A Multi-Source Data Fusion Approach across Diverse Chinese Basins

Abstract. The simulation of streamflow is a complex task due to its intricate formation process. Existing single models struggle to accurately capture the stochastic, non-stationary, and nonlinear dynamics of basin streamflow in changing environments. This study integrated process-driven hydrological mechanism models with data-driven deep learning models, considering various factors like hydrology, meteorology, environment, and the interconnected effects of upstream and downstream rivers, to form an interpretable hybrid streamflow simulation model. The study collected multiple external variables to better understand the hydrologic system complexity and used the Maximum Information Coefficient (MIC) to analyze their relationship with streamflow. Subsequently, the Xinanjiang (XAJ) model with physical mechanisms was employed, alongside the TCN-GRU model integrating Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), for separate streamflow simulations. Furthermore, a combined method was employed, achieving nonlinear ensemble through Random Forest (RF), resulting in the hybrid XAJ-TCN-GRU model. This model shows promising results in simulating streamflow in four different basins in China, achieving high Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE) values with 0.991, 0.971, 0.984, and 0.986 for the Wuding River, Chu River, Jianxi River, and Qingyi River respectively. In terms of streamflow simulation, flood simulating, and interval simulation, this model outperforms other benchmark models. Additionally, the study quantified the contributions of each hydro-meteorological variable to the long-term streamflow trend using mean absolute SHAP values (SHAPABS), Feature Importance (FI), and Permutation Feature Importance (PFI), thereby enhancing the model's external interpretability. The results of this study are of significant importance for optimizing water resource management and mitigating flood disasters.

Introduction Soil ranks among a nation’s most valuable natural assets, and reliable understanding of local soil resources is essential for effective land-use planning and rural development. Methods This study set out to evaluate soil fertility and quality across different land management practices in Sohag Governorate, Egypt, combining geoscience methods with the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS). GPS-located sampling covered 34 points spanning old cultivated, recently cultivated, and bare soils, and standard laboratory procedures were used to determine their physical and chemical properties. TOPSIS was then applied to each sample to derive a current fertility status and an overall soil quality index (SQI). Results and discussion The soil aggregate stability index (SASI) averaged 1.81 (range 1.14–2.57) in old cultivated soils, 1.36 (0.2–3.62) in recently cultivated soils, and 0.4 (0.08–1.67) in bare soils; the soil-sealing index (IB) averaged 1.32 (0.17–4.35), 1.40 (0.11–5.10) and 0.57 (0.44–1.09) for the same three groups, and the Forestier index (IF) averaged 1.74 (0.46–4.39), 1.69 (0.36–5.28) and 1.03 (0.66–1.64). Four fertility classes emerged from this analysis, occupying 4.21, 15.22, 15.36 and 65.21% of the surveyed land. SQI itself ranged from 36.36 to 52.00% in old cultivated soils, 28.13–53.57% in recently cultivated soils, and 2.94–25.00% in bare soils, resolving into three quality regions: a moderate-quality zone spanning old and recently cultivated land (55.64% of the study area), a poor-quality zone across parts of the recently cultivated and bare soils (35.47%), and a very-poor-quality zone concentrated in bare soils (8.89%). Conclusion Together, these results provide decision-makers and land managers a practical, spatially explicit basis for prioritizing soil conservation work. In arid agricultural contexts, identifying and mapping fertility-depleted zones in this manner creates the evidence base necessary for targeted rehabilitation, which is crucial for closing the yield gap, reducing dependence on food imports, and enhancing national food security.

Here, we show that cadmium sulfide transforms under flooded soil–rice conditions, releasing labile cadmium and increasing its bioavailability. In pot experiments, cadmium sulfide increased dissolved and extractable cadmium, altered bulk pore-water geochemistry, activated iron-regulated transporters, enhanced cadmium uptake, and elevated grain cadmium above food-safety limits. These findings reveal a soil-to-root transfer pathway in which phosphate-mediated immobilization provides only a partial sink and does not offset increased cadmium influx, highlighting the long-term food-safety risks of sulfide-based cadmium immobilization in flooded paddy soils. evidence_quotes: Diagnosing ecological risks under current land-use configurations in Inner Mongolia

China's food security strategy is shifting beyond cultivated land-based grain production toward diversified food sources and ecological sustainability. Grasslands play a critical role in this transition, supporting livestock production while providing multiple ecosystem services. However, agricultural intensification and cultivated land–grassland competition increasingly threaten their multifunctionality. Taking Inner Mongolia, a region that epitomizes these challenges, as a case study, this research develops a static ecological risk diagnostic framework under current (2024) land-use, integrating ecosystem service assessment and evaluation of land-use alignment with natural conditions. The results show that medium risk areas dominate Inner Mongolia (82.14%) and are primarily associated with ecosystem service-related risks. Among these, ecosystem services conflict on grasslands represents the largest share (58.97%), where high habitat quality co-occurs with low water yield and soil conservation. In terms of land-use alignment, although cultivated land is theoretically subject to broader natural constraints, a larger proportion of existing grassland lies within highly constrained environments. High risk areas further reveal contrasting risk patterns: cultivated land unsuitability is mainly associated with multiple ecosystem service deficiencies, whereas grassland vulnerability consistently co-occurs with ecosystem services conflict. These risk patterns imply different management priorities. High-risk cultivated land highlights the need for ecological restoration to recover ecosystem functionality, whereas widespread medium-risk grasslands call for landscape-scale enhancement of service synergies through region-specific and multi-stakeholder collaboration. The proposed framework provides a transferable approach for identifying restoration priorities and guiding sustainable land-use planning in Inner Mongolia and other agro-pastoral regions, supporting the coordinated achievement of both ecological and food security.

evidence_quotes: Soil Carbon Loss Driven by Soil Erosion: Progress, Challenges, and Future Directions

Soil-erosion-driven loss of soil organic carbon is a critical component of the global carbon cycle and climate change research. To systematically review the intellectual evolution and research frontiers in this field, this study employed bibliometric and knowledge mapping methods. It analyzed 8,814 relevant publications (8,707 from Web of Science and 107 from China National Knowledge Infrastructure) spanning January 1993 to July 2025. Results indicate that international research has shifted from early descriptions of erosion processes and carbon mobilization. Current focuses include precise quantification of carbon source or sink effects within the erosion–deposition continuum. Other priorities involve exploring multifactor coupling mechanisms and developing integrated modeling approaches. In contrast, domestic research in China has concentrated on empirical monitoring in representative regions. It also emphasizes evaluating the carbon sequestration effects of soil and water conservation measures. The innovation of this review lies in its comparative analysis, which systematically elucidates differences in scale emphasis and methodological pathways between international and domestic studies. An integrated analytical framework of “process–mechanism–effect–regulation” is proposed. This framework highlights future research priorities, including reducing uncertainties in multiscale estimation of erosion-driven carbon fluxes. It also emphasizes elucidating coupling mechanisms between biogeochemical processes and physical transport. Additionally, it focuses on assessing the carbon sequestration and emission reduction potential of nature-based solutions. This review aims to provide systematic scientific insights for advancing terrestrial carbon cycle theory and supporting regional ecological management.

Mapping this heterogeneity is therefore a pressing but underexplored need. We conclude that mapping geochemical domains is a fundamental tool for sustainable viticulture and recommend prioritizing the planting of new vineyards on volcanic soils to reduce fertilizer inputs and mitigate water stress under climate change.
